claim_ceiling: Cross-timescale envelope composition and synthetic signal-observability test only. No grid-code, transient stability, protection, inverter, islanding or real-world connection claim.

time_hierarchy.note: Coordination categories only. Actual control bandwidth, sample rate and protection settings must come from the qualified owner/OEM/grid operator.

synthetic_test_envelope_only.purpose: Demonstrate that average-load equality does not establish transient-envelope equivalence.

aliasing_calculation.interpretation: The 0.8 MW peak excursion and 8 MW/s ramp are compressed into a 0.444 kW difference in a 15-minute average; that average cannot qualify fast electrical behavior.

conditional_right.note: Illustrative conditional import grant only. Not firm capacity or a real grid agreement.

rules: Conditional import is not firm import.
A conditional right must be current, exact-resource-bound and authorized.
The measured response must meet the event's declared response deadline and rebound/service constraints.
A flexible-load response is demand response, not inverter-based grid support.
Grid-support or islanding claims require #3418/grid-owner evidence and applicable interconnection tests.

cases.mutation: Run steady 5.0 MW waveform with valid configuration and complete 1 ms samples.
Compare the steady and fast-event traces only by embedded 15-minute average.
Evaluate 5.8 MW peak and 8 MW/s ramp against fixture-only 0.5 MW / 5 MW/s event envelope.
Replace 1 ms source trace with 15-minute average only.
Remove samples 600–650 during event hold.
Set time alignment uncertainty greater than event edge duration.
Use 5.8 MW import against 5.0 MW firm limit without valid conditional grant.
Use the grant after valid_until.
Grant requires 1 MW curtailment in 10 seconds but candidate response arrives after 12 seconds.
Present compute workload reduction as inverter frequency/voltage support.
Claim voltage/frequency support without exact inverter, grid-owner and #3418 qualification report.
A shore-power schedule exists but #4448 commissioning/readiness evidence is absent.
Remove cloud/optimizer/federation while preserving local protection and operator control.
No grid-owner or OEM dynamic limit is supplied for exact configuration.
Declared contracted 10 MW resource responds fully within 6 seconds and sustains the declared reduction for 10 minutes, with special metering evidence.
Candidate response completes after 6 seconds for the Eskom IDR profile.
Declared demand-side reserve resource meets the published SAWEM 10-second full-response definition and 10-minute sustain duration, with Trading Unit/registration evidence.
Treat the Eskom six-second programme and the SAWEM ten-second definition as the same contract/profile.
A resource meets a 30-minute notice but can sustain only 90 minutes where the programme requires at least two hours.
Use 30-minute interval metering as the sole evidence for a six-second IDR response.
Promote published pre-feasibility spare substation capacity into contracted, qualified and available demand-response MW.
Treat mandatory emergency load reduction under NRS 048-9 as a voluntary contracted DR product.

target_hypotheses.caveat: Synthetic corpus targets only. Not measured performance, grid-code compliance or equipment qualification.

declared_terms.scheduling: scheduled day-ahead; dispatched on day when frequency reaches a preset level

limitations: Eligibility, connection, aggregation, telemetry, contractual availability and current procurement must be confirmed directly with Eskom.
10 MW programme minimum is not inferred from a port's reported spare grid headroom.
Do not treat the six-second response programme as the same product as the SAWEM instantaneous reserve definition.

declared_terms.resource_type: generating capacity or demand-side managed load
declared_terms.scheduling: day-ahead reserve category and real-time dispatch framework
declared_terms.payment: capacity qualifying and performance adjustment provisions exist in the code

limitations: Market Code Rev2.3 publication does not by itself establish that a particular port participant is registered, qualified or currently eligible.

NERSA's September 2026 regulatory tracker listed the Market Code approval workstream as finalisation with a target completion of 31 October 2026; the tracker snapshot is not evidence of the subsequent final regulatory decision.
The 10-second definition is distinct from Eskom Distribution's published 6-second IDR product.

declared_terms.minimum_entry_rule: max(500 kW, 15% of average plant demand)
declared_terms.maximum_frequency: once per day under the published description

limitations: Participant-specific contracted duration, activation, telemetry, settlement, aggregation and current availability must be confirmed with NTCSA/Eskom.
A 30-minute interval meter cannot alone demonstrate the separate six-second IDR performance requirement.
This is a slower supplemental product, not instantaneous reserve.

declared_terms.subject: emergency load reduction, load shedding, load curtailment and restoration

limitations: Emergency mandatory load reduction is not the same as a voluntary/contracted demand-response service.
Emergency instructions and authority remain with the relevant System Operator/utility; a scheduler cannot self-declare or override an emergency.
